To grind coarsely.
Something that has been kibbled, especially grain for use as animal feed.

examples.text: The pope had already signaled his kids-over-kibbles stance in a 2014 interview with the Rome daily Il Messaggero. When asked whether some in society valued pets more than children, he said that it was a reality that reflected a “sign of cultural degeneration.”

glosses: Any artificial animal feed in pellet form.
An iron bucket used in mines for hoisting anything to the surface.
A mallet used in the game of trap ball.
In the Transformers fandom, pieces of a toy or figure necessary for one mode, but appearing out of place or unnecessary in the other.
To strike (a person), originally with something flat or heavy, but now specifically in such a way as to discolour the skin without breaking it; to contuse.

examples.text: It is as I have spoken: the testing first, next the bruising, and in the last bout the breaking and killing.

glosses: To damage the skin of (fruit or vegetables), in an analogous way.
Of fruit or vegetables, to gain bruises through being handled roughly.
To become bruised.
To fight with the fists; to box.

examples.text: Bruising was considered a fine, manly, old English custom.

glosses: To harm or injure somebody's feelings or self-esteem.

examples.text: Her thoughtless remarks bruised my ego.
I was bruised by such wanton criticism.
